hook.text: In the 1970s, American cars broke down so often that owners joked 'Fix Or Repair Daily' about Ford.

buildup.text: Japanese cars weren't exciting, but they started every morning and rarely needed repairs.

discovery.text: The quality gap was measurable. Japanese cars had far fewer defects per vehicle off the assembly line.

twist.text: Detroit blamed cheap labor. The real reason was better processes—Toyota's methods, not Japan's wages.

climax.text: By the 1990s, reliability ratings became a major buying factor. Japan dominated every survey.

punchline.text: Reliability isn't glamorous, but it wins markets.

quiz.question: What was the real reason for Japanese car quality?
